'''Andrew James Baldwin''' (born February 5, 1977) is a [[United States Navy|U.S. Navy]] officer, ironman triathlete, television personality, [[humanitarian]], and [[physician]]. He appeared on the [[The Bachelor (American TV series) season 10|10th season]] of the reality dating show ''[[The Bachelor (American TV series)|The Bachelor]]''. He is currently married with one son.{{Infobox person

==Early life and education==
Baldwin was born on February 5, 1977, in [[Lancaster, Pennsylvania]], the son of [[Roy E. Baldwin]], a former two-term Pennsylvania State Representative (R-97th District), and Cynthia Laulani Baldwin, a high school mathematics teacher. He has a brother and sister.

Baldwin graduated as [[valedictorian]] of [[Manheim Township High School]] in 1995. He worked as a [[paper boy]], [[lifeguard]], and had his own lawn mowing business to earn money for college, saving $25,000 before graduating high school.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.midweek.com/content/story/Print_Story/roses_from_andy/|publisher=Midweek.com|title=Print Roses From Andy|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927043808/http://www.midweek.com/content/story/Print_Story/roses_from_andy/|archive-date=2007-09-27}}</ref> During high school, he played [[basketball]], [[tennis]], [[high school football|football]], [[baseball]], and was an [[All-American]] swimmer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.navycompass.com/sports/sportsview.asp?c=128728|title=Sports View|publisher=Navy Compass|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928210452/http://www.navycompass.com/sports/sportsview.asp?c=128728|archive-date=2007-09-28}}</ref> He was named [[ESPN]]'s National Scholar Athlete of the Year in 1995.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.militarymoney.com/columns/3/669|title = Choosing From Twenty-Five Women: Somebody's Got To Do It!|access-date = 2007-06-02|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070927062924/http://www.militarymoney.com/columns/3/669|archive-date = 2007-09-27|url-status = dead}}</ref>

Baldwin attended [[Duke University]], where he graduated ''[[magna cum laude]]'' in 1999 with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in [[biology]]. While at Duke, he was a varsity swimmer, member of the [[Pi Kappa Alpha]] fraternity, and a [[Navy Reserve Officer Training Corps]] [[midshipman]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://gohawaii.about.com/od/hawaii_media_guide/p/andy_baldwin.htm|title=U.S. Navy Lieutenant Andy Baldwin, M.D. – Hawaii's Own Officer and a Gentleman Stars in ABC TV's The Bachelor<!-- Bot generated title -->|access-date=2007-04-03|archive-date=2007-08-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070812233344/http://gohawaii.about.com/od/hawaii_media_guide/p/andy_baldwin.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uscpike.org/dynamic/?Action=show_custom_content&pageid=2262|title=Famous Pikes – USC Pi Kappa Alpha<!-- Bot generated title -->|access-date=2010-01-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091228100236/http://uscpike.org/dynamic/?Action=show_custom_content&pageid=2262|archive-date=2009-12-28|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduating from Duke University, Baldwin was commissioned an [[Ensign (rank)|ensign]] in the United States Navy and received a four-year [[Health Professions Scholarship Program|Navy Health Professions Scholarship]] to attend the [[UCSF School of Medicine|University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine]], receiving his [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] in 2003.<ref>[http://www.buddytv.com/articles/the-bachelor/profile/andy-baldwin.aspx Andy Baldwin<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> He subsequently completed an [[Medical intern#United States|internship]] in [[general surgery]] at the [[Naval Medical Center San Diego]], in 2004, and was a medical officer for Naval Special Warfare Group Three in Coronado from June to December 2004. He completed the Navy Undersea Medicine Training Institute and Navy Dive School in June 2005. In July 2005, he was given a three-year assignment as a member of the [[Navy Medical Corps]] to serve as Diving [[Medical Officer]] for Mobile Diving and Salvage Unit One in [[Pearl Harbor]], [[Oahu]], Hawaii.

On November 13, 2007, he told [[KITV]] that he was shortly to be deployed to [[Bahrain]]. ''[[Marianas Variety]]'', Micronesia's leading newspaper, recorded that he "is part of the [[Joint POW/MIA Accounting Command]] (JPAC) team conducting recovery operations in Palau."<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.mvariety.com/?module=displaystory&story_id=6100&format=html|title = Baldwin offers services in medical care|first = Bernadette H.|last = Carreon|date = February 3, 2008}}</ref>

In April 2008, Baldwin was transferred from Hawaii to [[Washington, D.C.]], where he is a Navy medicine advocate at the [[Bureau of Medicine and Surgery]].{{citation needed|date=March 2011}} In January 2009, Baldwin began working as assistant to the acting U.S. Surgeon General, RADM [[Steven Galson]] on his "Healthy Youth for a Healthy Future" initiative combating childhood overweight and obesity.<ref>[http://www.surgeongeneral.gov/news/pressreleases/pr20090518.html Acting Surgeon General Promotes “Healthy Youth for a Healthy Future” and National Physical Fitness and Sports Month in the Nation’s Capitol<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091014124959/http://www.surgeongeneral.gov/news/pressreleases/pr20090518.html|date=October 14, 2009}}</ref>

In March 2009, Baldwin was selected as a finalist but was not selected for the [[White House Fellows]] program.<ref>[https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the_press_office/The-White-House-Announces-Regional-Finalists-for-the-2009-2010-Class-of-White-House-Fellows/ The White House Announces Regional Finalists for the 2009–2010 Class of White House Fellows|The White House<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Baldwin is a Board Certified Family Physician and an MPH Graduate Student at the Johns Hopkins School of Public Health.<ref>[http://www.washingtonexaminer.com/politics/blogs/yeas-and-nays/Babes_-D_C_-loses-its-_Bachelor_-to-babies-1000175-98368034.html D.C. loses its 'Bachelor' to babies|Nikki Schwab|Yeas & Nays|Washington Examiner<!-- Bot generated title -->]{{Dead link|date=September 2018|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

===Humanitarian efforts===
[[File:US Navy 081106-N-8390S-016 Lt. Andrew Baldwin, M.D., assigned to the Navy Bureau of Medicine and Surgery, makes this patient and honorary Sailor at Shriners Hospital Houston.jpg|thumb|Baldwin visiting a patient in [[Shriners Hospital for Children (Houston)|Shriners Hospital for Children]] in [[Houston]]]]
Baldwin was awarded Humanitarian of the Year by Competitor Magazine at the Competitor Sports Awards. He was named to Outside magazine's top 100 influential people of the world list in 2006,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.competitorradio.com/details.php?show=132|title=Baldwin Named Humanitarian of the Year by Competitor Magazine|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080914010815/http://competitorradio.com/details.php?show=132|archive-date=2008-09-14}}</ref> and to the Washington, D.C. Most Influential People under 40 List in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://washingtonlife.com/2009/03/01/the-young-the-guest-list-2009/|title=The Young & the Guest List 2009|date=March 2009}}</ref>

Baldwin was awarded Triathlete Magazine Humanitarian of 2007 by Triathlete Magazine. Baldwin was also placed on ''[[Outside magazine|Outside]]'' magazine's list of the world's most influential people for the humanitarian work he did in [[Laos]] on a military mission where he treated over 600 Laotians in remote mountain villages for ailments such as malaria, dengue fever, parasites, and malnutrition. Baldwin also volunteered at the Aloha Medical Mission where he treated patients, free of charge, for various ailments.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.triathletemag.com/Departments/News/2007/LT_Andrew_Baldwin__M_D__receives_Triathlete_Magazine_Humanitarian_Award.htmBaldwin|title=Named Triathlete Magazine Humanitarian of 2007}}{{dead link|date=January 2017|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>
<!--
After the death of an uncle, Tom, from [[pancreatic cancer]], he established a fund to raise money for pancreatic cancer research. -->

Baldwin participated in ABC's ''[[Extreme Makeover: Home Edition]]'', building a new home for the Akana family in Hawaii.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.realitytvworld.com/news/bachelor-andy-baldwin-helps-abc-extreme-makeover-build-home-5319.php|title = Bachelor participates in Extreme Makeover Home Edition and builds a home for the Akana family in Hawaii}}</ref>

Baldwin established The Got Your Back Network, a nonprofit organization that raises money to support the families of the service men and women who gave their lives while serving their country.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Got Your Back Network - GuideStar Profile|url=https://www.guidestar.org/Profile/26-4819205|access-date=2024-04-12|website=www.guidestar.org}}</ref> 100% of the funds raised fund an endowment to provide financial support for applicant families: education, emergencies and medicine.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.gotyourbacknetwork.org/|title = Andy Baldwin's Got Your Back Network Organization}}</ref>

Baldwin is now focusing on more humanitarian works. He has been involved in numerous charities including the TV Special Stand Up to Cancer, winning the Malibu Triathlon raising money for the Children's Hospital Los Angeles,<ref>[http://www.nauticamalibutri.com/press.cfm?press_id=99 The 2011 Nautica Malibu Triathlon<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080926125037/http://www.nauticamalibutri.com/press.cfm?press_id=99|date=September 26, 2008}}</ref> [http://www.bestbuddies.org Best Buddies], [http://www.snowballexpress.org Snowball Express], etc.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.people.com/people/article/0,20228623,00.html|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120925220316/http://www.people.com/people/article/0,20228623,00.html|url-status = dead|archive-date = September 25, 2012|title = Andy Baldwin's New Reality: Philanthropy}}</ref>

==''The Bachelor''==
{{Further|The Bachelor (American TV series) season 10}}
Prior to being selected as a participant in ''The Bachelor'', Baldwin was featured as an eligible California bachelor in ''[[Cosmopolitan (magazine)|Cosmopolitan]]'' in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cosmopolitan.com/hot-guys/bachelors/05bachelors/CALIFORNIA_BACHELOR_O5/|title=Cosmo's California Bachelor 2005|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080505034745/http://www.cosmopolitan.com/hot-guys/bachelors/05bachelors/CALIFORNIA_BACHELOR_O5|archive-date=2008-05-05}}</ref>

The 10th season of the show, ''[[The Bachelor (American TV series) season 10|The Bachelor: Officer and a Gentleman]]'', premiered Monday, April 2, 2007, on the [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] television network. Baldwin proposed to [[Tessa Horst]] on the season finale, which aired May 21, 2007. She accepted his proposal. Eight months after the final episode, Horst broke up with Baldwin when he was on deployment in the Pacific.<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|url = http://www.realitytvworld.com/news/bachelor-couple-andy-baldwin-tessa-horst-break-off-engagement-5636.php|title = 'Bachelor' couple Andy Baldwin, Tessa Horst break off engagement|publisher = Reality TV World}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.etonline.com/slideshow/gallery/165551_bachelor_bachelorette_final_couples/2633|title='The Bachelor' and 'The Bachelorette' Romance Check! Which Couples Are Still Together? 'The Bachelor' Season 10 - Andrew Baldwin and Tessa Horst|author=ETonline Staff|publisher=Entertainment Tonight|access-date=April 29, 2020}}</ref>

In June 2008, ''[[People (magazine)|People]]'' named Andy Baldwin one of its hottest bachelors for 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.people.com/people/package/gallery/0,20205861_20205993_7,00.html|title = People Magazine named Andy Baldwin one of its Hottest Bachelors for 2008}}</ref>

==Other projects==
[[File:US Navy 080714-N-7006N-002 Lt. Andrew Baldwin, M.D., assigned to the Navy Bureau of Medicine and Surgery, speaks with Cassie Limpert about Navy Medicine and the medical opportunities the Navy has to offer during an airing of th.jpg|thumb|Baldwin in 2008]]
Honolulu Mayor Mufi Hannemann officially declared October 12 as Andy Baldwin Youth Fitness Day in the City and County of [[Honolulu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.crossoverentertainment.com/Client-AndyBaldwin.php|title=Andy Baldwin Youth Fitness Day Declared in Hawaii|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081215160254/http://www.crossoverentertainment.com/Client-AndyBaldwin.php|archive-date=2008-12-15}}</ref>

In October 2009, Baldwin led a Health Ride across [[Pennsylvania]] with his father, speaking at elementary schools about the importance of physical activity.<ref>[http://www.healthride.org Kidz Nation NetWork<!-- Bot generated title -->]  {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100111140850/http://www.healthride.org/|date=January 11, 2010}}</ref>

Baldwin is the founder of Got Your Back Network, an organization that assists military families who have lost a spouse or parent in [[Operation Iraqi Freedom]] or [[Operation Enduring Freedom]]. The goal of Got Your Back Network is to "give comfort, answer a special need, offer guidance and bring a brighter day to these families."<ref>[http://www.gotyourbacknetwork.org Got Your Back Network, Providing services to families of fallen soldiers through special events & organizations<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

On May 30, 2010, Baldwin ran 56 miles in [[South Africa]], the Comrades Ultramarathon, as key member of Team World Vision securing sponsorships for children in need in Africa, Haiti, and other underdeveloped countries.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.worldvision.org/content.nsf/pages/team-world-vision-comrades-marathon|title=Comrades Marathon|publisher=World Vision|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100207150947/http://www.worldvision.org/content.nsf/pages/team-world-vision-comrades-marathon|archive-date=2010-02-07}}</ref>

In June 2010, Baldwin made an appearance on the premiere of ''[[Top Chef]]'' in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref>[http://popwatch.ew.com/2010/06/17/top-chef-premiere-recap-washington-d-c-its-paradise-to-me/ 'Top Chef' premiere recap: Washington D.C., it's paradise to me|PopWatch|EW.com<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref>

On February 1, 2011, Baldwin was named National Ambassador for the ING Kids Rock running program which gets kids involved in running and helps fight childhood obesity.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120729141818/http://www.environmental-expert.com/resultEachPressRelease.aspx?cid=40439&codi=222388|title=ING and the Competitor Group Align to launch kids running series on Environmental Expert}}</ref>

==Triathlons==
[[File:US Navy 070427-N-4856G-024 Lt. (Dr.) Andrew Baldwin, of Lancaster, Pa., stationed at Mobile Diving and Salvage Unit (MDSU) 1, holds his breath after being dunked.jpg|thumb|Baldwin in a dunk tank during a 2007 U.S. Navy event]]
Baldwin has been named to the All-Navy triathlon team five times, been a three-time U.S.A. Triathlon All-American, and competed internationally in numerous Half-Ironman and Ironman events. He is an eight-time Ironman finisher.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://navymemorial.ibelong.com/Pages/Layouts/GroupPage.aspx?SiteId=2178&PersistentTheme=navy|title=Baldwin Named to the All-Navy Triathlon Team Five Times|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081005073804/http://navymemorial.ibelong.com/Pages/Layouts/GroupPage.aspx?SiteId=2178&PersistentTheme=navy|archive-date=2008-10-05}}</ref> In addition, he completed the [[2013 New York City Marathon]] with a time of 3:18:13.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.runnersworld.com/runners-stories/a20830660/how-notable-runners-fared-at-the-2014-new-york-city-marathon/|title=How Notable Runners Fared at the 2014 New York City Marathon|last=Hetzel|first=Megan|date=2014-11-02|website=Runner's World|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-16}}</ref>

In 2015, Challenge Family Triathlons announced its partnership with Dr. Andy Baldwin. He will serve as an ambassador for the brand and compete in Challenge Family Americas races Challenge Family Americas board member Charlie Patten insists, “Andy is the real deal' a humanitarian and health care provider who serves his country and the world at large with generosity of heart and an indomitable spirit, lending a caring hand to US veterans and delivering critical medical care to those in need around the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://triathlonmagazine.ca/news/former-bachelor-and-humanitarian-dr-andy-baldwin-partners-with-challenge-family-americas/|title=Former reality TV star Dr. Andy Baldwin partners with Challenge Family Americas|date=2015-04-09|website=Triathlon Magazine Canada|language=en-CA|access-date=2020-01-16}}</ref>

In 2024, Professional Triathletes Organization named Dr. Baldwin its first Medical Director. In this role, Dr. Baldwin will oversee the coordination and implementation of PTO’s Medical Team programs, ensuring uniformity in the execution of the PTO’s medical plan and continuity of care and service across all events. He will also collaborate closely with World Triathlon to align PTO’s policies, procedures, and protocols with those of the global triathlon community.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://protriathletes.org/fr/media-releases/pto-appoint-dr-andy-baldwin-as-medical-director/ | title=Professional Triathletes Organisation Appoints Dr Andy Baldwin as Medical Director }}</ref>
